cards.body:
## Summary
The rule 'how a staged inbound envelope becomes applied or rejected' is implemented twice: once in the wallet runtime (batched, one audit row per deal+generation, C-9b) and once in the HOUSE tick (one audit row per message, tick-aborting on a ledger error). Move it into one `Wallet::drain_inbox(now, classify)` in table-app; both callers supply only their per-message policy.

## Description
`crates/table-app/src/relay.rs` gains `drain_inbox`, which owns: reading `pending_inbox`, the stored-hash duplicate shortcut, calling a caller-supplied `classify(&mut Wallet, &InboxMessage) -> Inbound {Apply, Reject, Retry(Error)}`, finishing applied rows, collecting rejected rows and writing them with `reject_inbox` once per deal+generation, and the Sql/Integrity stop. The runtime's closure keeps `select_signer` / `mandate_retired` / receipt pass-through; its `close_groups` call stays after the pass. The HOUSE's closure is today's `Seller::receive` (off-schedule OFFER -> `record_declined_offer`, else `receive_relay`). C-9c closes as a consequence, and the HOUSE gets the inbox test harness STATUS asked for.

## Flow
- table-app: add `Inbound` + `Wallet::drain_inbox`; tests in `crates/table-app/tests/inbox.rs` drive it over a real ledger.
- runtime: `consume_inbox` becomes the closure + `drain_inbox` + `close_groups`.
- HOUSE: the `pending_inbox` loop in `Seller::tick` becomes one `drain_inbox` call wrapped in `noted("inbox", ...)`; a returned error is recorded as the tick's failure instead of returning early, so negotiate and report_pending still run.
- house_tests: junk-batch and two-deal cases.

## Expected impact
One place decides inbox accounting for every party; a future rule (C-9a-style caps, retired-mandate handling) lands once. The public HOUSE record stops growing one row per junk message a hostile buyer posts (up to 256 per mailbox generation).

## Evaluation
Claim: one inbox pass gives the HOUSE the wallet's batched rejection and removes the duplicated loop.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass as written (cases 1, 2 fail on per-message rows; 4-6 have no shared API; 7 trivially passes but is the regression guard)
After: 7 of 7 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked hosted.rs:653-687 and ledger relay.rs:279-340 for cases 1-3, runtime relay.rs:124-206 for 4-7; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: architecture (a new shared table-app API both binaries call; no wire, audit-shape or migration change)

cards.body:
## Summary
The scoreboard claims 'The record never got shorter' but cannot tell a rewritten-then-extended record from an honest one, and a buyer holding the house's signed head (in their wallet or proof file) has no way to check it without installing the CLI. The house already signs prefixes for exactly this. Make the page a witness: each visit proves the current record extends the last look, any visitor can drop in a kept head or proof file and get Extends / Rewritten / New record in seconds, and any look can be saved as a signed head the offline checker accepts.

## Description
A pure `witness.js` (classic script, loaded before scoreboard.js under the existing CSP, also importable by node tests) holds `compareHeads` (the Rust table, case for case), `prefixToAsk`, `keptHeadsFrom` (bare SignedHouseHead or a table.proof.v2 bundle's `house.heads`), `witnessVerdict` and `lookToSave`. scoreboard.js: checkHeads asks `/v1/house/prefix?rows=N` for the newest shorter look, verifies the prefix signature with WebCrypto over canonical(["table.house.prefix.v1", prefix]), and words the result ('Extends what this browser saw at 14:02, signed by the house'). The 'Check it yourself' card gains 'Check a head you kept' (file input, read locally, never uploaded) listing one verdict per head, and 'Save this look'.

## Flow
- Visitor returns -> page fetches ledger, then one prefix at the last shorter look -> check line reads Extends (ok) / Rewritten (bad) / Longer (unknown, when Ed25519 is missing).
- Buyer drops their proof file -> each kept head verified against the release agent key -> prefix fetched at its row count -> per-head verdict, receipt head first.
- Save this look -> downloads house-head-<rows>.json usable as `table-verify --house ... --head <file>`.

## Expected impact
The page's strongest claim becomes true rather than local-only, and the buyer witness the wallet runs every 15 minutes becomes something any judge can do in one drop, without the desktop app or the CLI.

## Evaluation
Claim: the page proves extension, not just non-shrinkage, and checks heads it did not see itself.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no witness module, no prefix fetch, looks unsigned, no asset route)
After: 7 of 7 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked compare_heads (house_ledger.rs:139-171) against each case, and checkHeads (scoreboard.js:241-258) for the rewritten-and-longer case it passes today; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: none (read-only public page; an existing route; no wire or contract change)
